title: Why Recycling Plants Never Open Garbage Bags #shorts
summary: At a material recovery facility, tied garbage bags are never opened, for the workers' safety, so whatever is inside goes to landfill; loose plastic bags are pulled by hand before the machines (City of Calgary). On average 15-20% of what is collected curbside is not recyclable (National Academies, 2025).
sources: How a material recovery facility sorts a blue cart: trucks unload, workers pre-sort plastic bags and hazardous items by hand, disc screens lift cardboard and flat paper, a glass breaker shatters glass so it falls through a screen and a cyclone lifts lighter paper and plastic off it, optical sorters with air jets, a magnet picks up tin cans, an eddy current 'acts like a magnet in reverse' and repels foil, cans and pie plates onto another belt, sorted material is baled and sold; '90% automated sorting by machines', 'the other 10% is handled manually'; 'garbage bags are never opened during the sorting process'; destinations: plastics to Canada, metal cans and foil to Eastern Canada, cardboard to Canada and the US, paper to Eastern Canada, the US, India, Malaysia and Taiwan, glass to Western Canada (City of Calgary, How the recycling facility works): https://www.calgary.ca/uep/wrs/recycling-information/residential-services/blue-cart-recycling/how-recycling-works.html

Much of the material collected in recycling programs is directed to about 500 MRFs; contamination, the amount of nonrecyclables collected curbside, is 15-20 percent on average; a typical MRF captures about 87 percent of its incoming accepted program recyclable materials (National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine, Municipal Solid Waste Recycling in the United States: Analysis of Current and Alternative Approaches, 2025, ch. 2): https://www.nationalacademies.org/read/27978/chapter/4

scenes.narration: At a recycling plant, a tied garbage bag is never opened.
It's for the workers' safety. Whatever is inside goes to landfill.
Loose plastic bags get pulled off the line by hand, before the machines.
On average, {15 to 20%|fifteen to twenty percent} of what's collected at the curb can't be recycled there.
